Team — draft answers below (I also attached the artifacts referenced). Please review and flag any edits. I kept language concise for procurement. Attachments: redwood_vpc_network_diagram_v1.pdf, deployment_playbook_excerpt.txt, kms_integration_matrix.xlsx, soc2_cert_redacted.pdf

1) Air-gapped on-prem package: Yes. Redwood offers a fully air-gapped installer that contains runtime, model artifacts, and a local control-plane. No mandatory outbound connections are required for inference. Optional connectivity:
- License activation: we support both online activation and offline token-based activation. For fully air-gapped customers we ship signed license tokens and an offline activation flow (no callbacks to redwood).
- Telemetry: Telemetry is opt-in; for air-gapped deployments telemetry is disabled by default. Support bundles can be exported and uploaded via customer-controlled media.

2) Recommended per-store VPC architecture (summary):
- Each store runs a dedicated VPC/subnet with private worker nodes and a management bastion in a separate management VPC.
- Required inbound/outbound: primarily SSH (for management) on bastion; inference traffic is local to store. If replication or model sync needed, we recommend a scheduled egress window via NAT gateway or a sync proxy.
- Cross-VPC routing: Support via VPC peering or Transit Gateway; avoid flattening store traffic across sites unless forced. See attached diagram for port lists and CIDR examples.

3) KMS/HSM options:
- Customer-managed KMS (preferred): integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or on-prem HSM using PKCS#11. We provide an HSM connector shim; see kms_integration_matrix.xlsx for supported providers and required configurations.
- Redwoods-managed key escrow: available under strict contract (not default for enterprise air-gapped installs).

4) Evidence for patching/SBOM:
- We provide (1) a signed SBOM for each release, (2) patch notes with CVE mapping, and (3) optional quarterly attestation reports. SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) attached. For on-prem packages we include checksums and signed manifests for binary provenance.

5) Hardware/driver constraints:
- Supported drivers: we publish a matrix. Short list: NVIDIA driver >=470 for Ampere; CUDA 11.3+ recommended. Some older GPU families require specific runtime builds; see attachment for full matrix.

6) Rollback & incident playbook (high-level):
- Detection: health checks and KV-cache integrity scans.
- Isolation: mark node as read-only and divert traffic to regional fallback model variant.
- Restore: rehydrate model files from local signed artifact store and validate checksums.
- Postmortem: collect local logs (support bundle) and perform integrity attestation; escalate to Redwood security if compromise suspected.

Notes: We also include a short customer-runbook excerpt (deployment_playbook_excerpt.txt) that covers update cadence and recommended maintenance windows.

Vanessa
